title: Majestic Misplacement
summary: Improve the king before exchanging bishops, then deflect the opposing king so promotion wins with tempo.

nodes.question: Why delay the immediate promotion?
nodes.explanation: White can exchange the b-pawn for Black’s bishop, but the king must first deny Black access to b6.

nodes.question: How can White win the pawn race?
nodes.explanation: Both pawns are close to promotion. The bishop can change the black king’s position before the race begins.

branches.title: Prepare the king, then sacrifice for a skewer
commentary: Begin after ...Ba7 declines the first bishop sacrifice. The b7 pawn is attacked, but White has time for a king move.
Ka5 controls b6. White removes the defensive king route before liquidating the bishops.
d4 advances Black’s counterplay. This is the source’s selected reply, not the only legal defense.
b8=Q offers the promoted queen to eliminate the black bishop.
Bxb8 captures the queen. Black exchanges the bishop for the b-pawn.
Bxb8 recaptures. White keeps the bishop and the a-pawn, but must still stop the d-pawn.
d3 brings Black within two moves of promotion. Racing immediately would throw away the win.
Bd6+ forces the king to address a checking bishop sacrifice. Its destination determines the promotion tactics.
Kxd6 accepts the bishop and places the king on the d-file, in front of its own future queen.
a7 starts the promotion race now that the king has been deflected.
d2 keeps Black’s counter-promotion threat alive.
a8=Q gets White a queen first. The important point is the coming alignment on the d-file.
d1=Q also promotes, but Black’s king on d6 is vulnerable to a skewer.
Qd8+ checks along the d-file. Once the king leaves that file, White takes the queen on d1; the tablebase confirms the winning endpoint.
branches.explanation: Qd8+ checks along the d-file. Once the king leaves that file, White takes the queen on d1; the tablebase confirms the winning endpoint.

branches.title: Promote before improving the king
commentary: Compare the same bishop exchange while White’s king still stands on a4.
b8=Q is the actual error: without Ka5, the resulting bishop-and-rook-pawn ending is drawn.
Bxb8 removes the promoted queen as before.
Bxb8 leaves White with an extra bishop, but that bishop does not control the a8 promotion square.
Kb6 uses the route White failed to cover and attacks a6.
a7 saves the pawn from capture, but gives Black time to occupy its promotion corner.
Kb7 reaches the defensive corner route. White’s light-squared bishop cannot drive the king from the dark promotion square; this position is a checked draw.
branches.explanation: Kb7 reaches the defensive corner route. White’s light-squared bishop cannot drive the king from the dark promotion square; this position is a checked draw.

branches.title: Race without deflecting the king
commentary: White’s extra bishop does not automatically decide a queen ending. Check the timing before advancing.
a7 gives up the forced win by starting the race too early.
d2 keeps pace while the king remains safely away from the d-file skewer.
a8=Q promotes first, but no decisive check interrupts Black’s reply.
d1=Q gives Black a queen without placing its king in front of it. The exact resulting queen-and-bishop ending is drawn with best play.
branches.explanation: d1=Q gives Black a queen without placing its king in front of it. The exact resulting queen-and-bishop ending is drawn with best play.

branches.title: If the king declines the sacrifice
commentary: The sacrifice also has a positional point if Black refuses to capture the bishop.
Bd6+ checks and offers the bishop. White wants the king away from the a8 corner.
Kc4 declines the capture and walks away from the promotion corner.
Bf4 controls d2, stopping the pawn’s next step. The king on c4 is too far away to recreate the earlier corner defense; White retains a checked win.
branches.explanation: Bf4 controls d2, stopping the pawn’s next step. The king on c4 is too far away to recreate the earlier corner defense; White retains a checked win.

exercises.prompt: What does Ka5 accomplish that a promotion cannot?
exercises.answer: It denies ...Kb6 before the bishop exchange. The wrong-colored bishop cannot win if Black reaches the a8 corner.

exercises.prompt: Why does giving up the bishop improve the pawn race?
exercises.answer: After ...Kxd6 the king stands in front of its future queen, so Qd8+ skewers them. After ...Kc4, Bf4 stops the pawn while the king is too far from the corner.

startContext: Begin after ...Ba7 at 21 seconds. The preceding Bc7 sacrifice remains source context. The selected king preparation, drawing errors and bishop deflection are checked here.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
